---
title: "multised (refined)"
subtitle: "The refined marine-sediment database and the analyses built on it"
---

**multised** assembles a database of marine-sediment trace-element measurements from
five external sources, harmonises them into a common schema, and progressively
quality-controls the result. This site presents the **refined** database: an
analysis-ready version of the merged database, restructured and slimmed with the
reusable results of the earlier analyses baked in, together with the analyses built on
it.

The refined database is purpose-built for identifying **pristine / background
sediments**, sediment relatively unaffected by local pressure, so that concentrations
elsewhere can be judged against a natural baseline. It bakes in the values those
analyses reuse (the Fe / Al and organic-carbon ratios, the grain-size fines, the
aquaculture link and the repeat-sampling grouping) and leaves the classifications
themselves (enrichment factors, thresholds, the pristine label) to the analyses.

## The database

A single database, `multised_refined.sqlite`. It holds the 7 target elements in one
`measurement` table (bulk and sieved told apart by `frac_class`) with the Fe / Al /
organic ratios baked in, a slim `normaliser` table, and the repeat-sampling grouping on
the sites. The Norwegian **aquaculture** reference is now a table **inside** this
database (each Norwegian sediment site links to its nearest farm by `site.aqua_id`), so
there is no separate aquaculture file.

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(knitr)

tribble(
  ~Table,        ~Contents,
  "measurement", "The 7 target elements (CO CU I MN MO SE ZN), bulk and sieved by frac_class, with ratio_fe / ratio_al / ratio_corg baked in.",
  "normaliser",  "Fe / Al / organic carbon per subsample and fraction (the ratio denominators).",
  "site",        "Locations, with the geo-enrichment, the aquaculture link (aqua_id) and the repeat-sampling grouping (repeat_group, n_years).",
  "aquaculture", "Norwegian marine aquaculture sites (active and closed), linked from site.aqua_id.",
  "subsample / event / dataset / element / method", "The supporting dimensions (depth slices, sampling events, campaigns, the element lookup and analytical methods)."
) |> kable()
```

## Pipeline generations

The data moves through five generations, one SQLite database **per source** until the
merge, then a single database from there:

1. **pilot**: each source's raw files parsed into a per-source database. Documented on
   the individual pilot sites:
   [Mareano](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mareano-pilot/),
   [Vannmiljø](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/vannmiljo-pilot/),
   [ICES-DOME](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/ices-dome-pilot/),
   [MUDAB](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mudab-pilot/), and
   [4Demon](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/4demon-pilot/).
2. **slim**: every source reshaped into the same seven-table schema, then annotated
   with quality-control flags. Documented on the
   [slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/).
3. **clean**: the flags are applied (uncertain rows removed), units harmonised, and
   grain-size split into its own table. Five per-source databases. Documented on the
   [clean-analyses site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-clean/).
4. **merged**: the five clean databases are combined into a single database, with
   cross-source duplicates removed. Its build is documented on the
   [merged site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-merged/).
5. **refined** *(this site)*: a restructured, slimmed copy of the merged database with
   the reusable analysis results baked in, an analysis-ready base for the pristine /
   background-sediment work, and the analyses performed on it.

## What this site covers

**DB Design**

- [DB Schema](./db-schema-refined.qmd): the table layout of the refined database (all
  its tables, including the aquaculture reference), with an entity-relationship diagram.
- [Tables](./refined-tables.qmd): a read-only browser over the database, running in your
  browser via WebAssembly.

**Background** on the refined database, four aquaculture-free ways to estimate a natural
baseline per element and fraction:

- [Global Background](./background.qmd): a natural background per element and fraction, the
  global distribution versus an offshore subset.
- [Grain-Size-Normalised Background](./background-gsnorm.qmd): the same after removing
  the grain-size effect, normalised three ways (metal/Al, metal/Fe, metal/mud).
- [Distribution-Mixture Background](./background-mixture.qmd): separating a background
  population from an enriched one from the distribution alone, and checking it against
  the spatial background.
- [Pressure-Based Background](./background-pressure.qmd): background from distance to
  aquaculture, and the near-cage enrichment (Norway), used to evaluate the enrichment.
- [Pressure Controls](./pressure-controls.qmd): what is left of that near-cage enrichment
  once the comparison is matched within a municipality and restricted to samples taken while
  the farm was operating. Copper and zinc lose almost all of it.
- [Background Map](./background-map.qmd): all sites in grey with the offshore, below-P90
  and below-mixture background samples overlaid, per element and fraction.
- [Background Summary](./background-summary.qmd): the four estimates side by side per
  element and fraction, how far apart they are, and which value to use for each element.
  **Start here if you want a number.**

**Enrichment**, turning the background into a per-sample verdict, with the aquaculture
pressure held back for evaluation:

- [Enrichment Factor](./background-ef.qmd): classifying samples against a local (offshore,
  aquaculture-free) background (EF), then testing whether the reported enrichment matches
  the aquaculture pressure gradient.
- [Regression Normalisation](./background-regression.qmd): whether the ratio's
  through-the-origin assumption matters here (it does not), and whether aluminium predicts
  each metal at all. It does for cobalt, copper and zinc in bulk and for nothing else, which
  is why those are the only groups that carry an enrichment factor. The test governs bulk
  only: a sieved sample was grain-size controlled by the sieve before the chemistry, so it
  is judged without one.
- [Pristine Classification](./background-pristine.qmd): combining the background estimates
  into a per-sample verdict (using no aquaculture information), checked against distance
  to the cages, and noting where it cannot be made (the bulk samples around the farms lack
  the aluminium needed, because the programme that collects them does not report it). The
  sieved fractions are judged on the sieve instead, against their own offshore reference.
- [Method Revisions](./method-revisions.qmd): what changed in the background and pristine
  methods, what forced each change, and which figures moved. Read this first if you hold a
  download taken before v0.9.0.
- [Enrichment Map](./enrichment-map.qmd): all sites in grey with the potentially pristine
  samples (EF and strict) overlaid, per element and fraction.
- [Enrichment Summary](./enrichment-summary.qmd): how enriched the collection is under both
  EF references, how much of it can be judged at all, and whether the verdicts survive the
  held-out aquaculture check. **Start here if you want the conclusion.**

A multi-element pollution index may be added later.

**EFSA Submission**, the reporting formats this collection is meant to feed, and what the
refined database can put into each of their columns:

- [EFSA Format v1](./efsa-format.qmd) and [EFSA Format v2](./efsa-format-v2.qmd): the
  column definitions and catalogues of the EFSA reporting tool and of the later FHF marine
  sediment data model. These describe the formats themselves, so they are the same on every
  site in this project.
- [EFSA Submission v1](./efsa-submission.qmd) and
  [EFSA Submission v2](./efsa-submission-v2.qmd): the mapping from the refined tables onto
  those columns, with the share of measurements that can fill each one, and the two
  constraints (sampling year, and an EF-based pristine verdict that needs aluminium, so
  bulk only) that cut the collection down before any of it is submitted.

**Downloads**

- [Database](./download-database.qmd): the full refined database as a single SQLite file.
- [Dataset](./download-dataset.qmd): a flat, denormalised table (tsv.gz) of just the values
  needed for background and enrichment work, one row per measurement, with a description of
  every column.

::: {.callout-note}
How the refined database is assembled from the merged database, step by step (the
restructure, the normaliser, the baked ratios, the aquaculture and repeat-sampling
links), is documented on the
[merged site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-merged/) under **Refined DB**.
:::
